title: On Shifting the load to the other shoulder
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：shift　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 shift 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the builder ① shifted the load to the other shoulder before dawn, and every assistant in the site said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the builder ② shifts the load to the other shoulder in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ shift the load to the other shoulder at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ shifted the load to the other shoulder before — a line in the plan for October 1984 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Shifting the load to the other shoulder before dawn, the builder said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the beam at the far wall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ shift the meeting to the following week in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Shift the meeting to the following week at once and never mention it again.

By 1997 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the plan, and a new assistant from the next site ⑧ shifts the meeting to the following week before dawn every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the wall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ shifted the load to the other shoulder again when nobody else would.

⑩ To shift the load to the other shoulder, my mother said in 2002, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the site remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the site forgets, somebody shifts the load to the other shoulder in public again and somebody must shift the load to the other shoulder before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 转移（一般过去式 shifted the load to the other shoulder：1990 年施工员头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 转移（一般现在 shifts the load to the other shoulder：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 转移（不定式 to shift the load to the other shoulder：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 转移（过去完成时 had shifted the load to the other shoulder：1984 年十月的施工图上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 转移（动名词 shifting the load to the other shoulder 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 改变（shift the meeting to the following week：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去改变把聚会改到下一周）
G. v. 改变（shift the meeting to the following week：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 转移（后段两处：新来的帮工照例 shifts the meeting to the following week，而母亲又一次 shifted the load to the other shoulder）

answers.why: shift 意为“转移”，1990 年施工员天没亮就转移把担子换到另一边肩上，那是工地里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 shifted。
shift 意为“转移”，自那以后施工员当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 shifts。
shift 意为“转移”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯转移把担子换到另一边肩上”，此处为不定式 to shift the load to the other shoulder。
shift 意为“转移”，施工图里 十月 那行字说明早在 1997 年之前就有人转移过，故用过去完成时 had shifted。
shift 意为“转移”，施工员说“转移把担子换到另一边肩上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 shifting the load to the other shoulder 作主语。
shift 意为“改变”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去改变把聚会改到下一周”，should ever 之后用原形 shift the meeting to the following week。
shift 意为“改变”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻改变把聚会改到下一周（shift the meeting to the following week at once），以后再也不要提起。
shift 意为“转移”，新来的帮工每个月份都照例改变把聚会改到下一周，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 shifts。
shift 意为“转移”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就转移把担子换到另一边肩上，用一般过去式 shifted 叙述。
shift 意为“转移”，结尾那句是母亲 2002 年的话：要转移把担子换到另一边肩上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工地记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 shift 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the builder shifted the load to the other shoulder before dawn, and nobody in the site forgot it.
Even now the builder shifts the load to the other shoulder in public whenever the site asks.
Shifting the load to the other shoulder before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever shift the meeting to the following week in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new assistant from the next site shifts the meeting to the following week before dawn every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother shifted the load to the other shoulder again, and the site remembered that half.
